title: Pilot study comparing two digital optical axiography systems with regard to the agreement of mandibular movement patterns and static occlusal contacts
summary:
Axiography (or jaw tracking) systems are special devices used to precisely record the movements of the lower jaw, particularly in the jaw joints. This allows movement patterns to be displayed and analyzed in three dimensions. Such measurements support the diagnosis of functional disorders, the planning of dental restorations or splints, and the monitoring of treatment progress.

There are two main types of systems:
- Conventional electronic jaw tracking uses mechanical devices attached to the head to record jaw movements mechanically or digitally. This method has been used for decades, is reliable, but can be time-consuming and less comfortable for patients.
- Digital optical jaw tracking uses cameras and sensors to capture jaw movements with high precision in three dimensions. These systems are often more comfortable, provide results more quickly, and can be seamlessly integrated into digital workflows. They can also virtually display tooth contacts during jaw movements – a technique known as a “virtual / real-dynamic articulator.”
Previous studies have mostly compared individual measurement values, such as the inclination of the condylar path or the so-called Bennett angle, between the two methods. Results generally show good agreement, with minor variations depending on the device.
However, there is little scientific data comparing the complete movement patterns of the lower jaw or the virtual simulation of tooth contacts between different digital systems.
The aim of this study is to assess the accuracy and agreement of various digital optical jaw tracking systems 
• ModJaw (ModJaw, Villeurbanne, Frankreich)
• JMA-Optic (Zebris Medical GmbH, Isny, Deutschland)
with each other and in comparison to conventional electronic systems. This will help determine how well these methods can be used for diagnosis and treatment planning in dentistry.

interventions.name:
Examination of all study participants using
- ModJaw (ModJaw, Villeurbanne, France)
- JMA-Optic (Zebris Medical GmbH, Isny, Germany)
at a single examination appointment in randomized order.
